options.text: Timing how long the fizzing lasts is useful evidence of the change.
Noting whether bubbles formed is useful evidence, even though it is only yes or no.
The brand name printed on the baking soda packet is useful evidence of the change in the cup.
A yes-or-no observation cannot count as evidence.

stem:
Shaurya mixes baking soda with vinegar in a steel cup. The mixture fizzes and feels cooler. He wants evidence to make sense of the changes.

Which claims about useful evidence are correct? One or more options may be correct.

teacher.key_rationale: Timed fizzing and whether bubbles formed are observable results of the change. Packet brand names are not evidence of the reaction, and yes/no observations can still be evidence.
